recommendation: Product DNA partial-update fields are `T | null` (present+null clears, key omitted carries forward); Json-typed nullable columns route explicit null through the Prisma.JsonNull sentinel rather than a literal null.
alternatives: Treat `{field: undefined}` as a third distinct state meaning 'clear'
Accept literal null directly in Prisma create data for Json columns
reason: Caught during implementation: TypeScript strict mode rejected passing literal `null` into Prisma's generated create input for nullable Json columns, which require the `Prisma.JsonNull` sentinel to disambiguate 'set to JSON null' from 'field not provided'. Separately, an initial test used `{productEdge: undefined}` expecting carry-forward semantics, but `"field" in {field: undefined}` is true in JS, so the merge logic would have treated it as an explicit (empty) write, not an omission — silently violating the Master Spec §10 'must not silently erase' requirement for that edge case. Fixed by making the public contract only recognize two states (key omitted = carry forward, key present with null = clear) and never treating undefined-but-present as meaningful.
impact: src/lib/product/product-dna.ts and its tests; establishes the pattern for any future versioned/mergeable model.
risk: Low — caught by strict typecheck and corrected before commit; both states now have dedicated passing tests (EV-0013).
customerResponse: n/a — routine technical decision, root-caused per Execution Protocol §9.

recommendation: Impact Analysis keyword matching uses left-anchored word-boundary regex (\bkeyword) rather than plain substring .includes() or full-word-boundary (\bkeyword\b) matching.
alternatives: Plain .includes() substring matching
Full \bkeyword\b (both edges anchored)
reason: Caught a real bug during implementation: plain .includes() matching flagged "Build a premium booking app for mobile detailers." as touching the 'screens' category, because "build" contains the substring "ui" (the keyword for screens). Fixed with full \b...\b boundaries first, which then caused a false negative: \bdeposit\b does not match "deposits" because there's no boundary between "deposit" and the trailing "s". Settled on left-boundary-only matching (\bkeyword, no trailing \b), which rejects the original false positive (no word boundary exists before "ui" inside "build") while still matching ordinary inflections like "deposits" and "memberships". Both regressions are covered by dedicated tests.
impact: src/lib/orchestration/impact-analysis.ts. This is explicitly documented as a deterministic foundation to be replaced by real graph-based impact analysis once Phase 2 populates Product Knowledge relationships with real Workflow/Screen/etc. nodes — imprecision here is bounded and disclosed, not hidden.
risk: Low — some over-matching on short keyword prefixes remains possible (e.g. "fee" would match "feed"), acceptable for a foundation-tier heuristic that never gates anything more consequential than a disclosure-tier default.
customerResponse: n/a — routine technical decision, root-caused per Execution Protocol §9.

recommendation: Truth Status maps a capability's platform-level implementationLevel to a conservative per-project status: SUPPORTED_NOW->IMPLEMENTED, SUPPORTED_WITH_*/SUPPORTED_LATER_PHASE/PROTOTYPE_ONLY/PLANNING_ONLY->PLANNED, EXTERNAL_APPROVAL_REQUIRED/PROFESSIONAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED->BLOCKED, NOT_CURRENTLY_SUPPORTED/UNSAFE_OR_PROHIBITED->UNSUPPORTED, INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION or no registry entry->NOT_EVALUATED. Every Truth Status entry is backed by a ProductEvidence record it references via evidenceRef.
alternatives: Treat SUPPORTED_NOW on the platform registry as IMPLEMENTED for every project that references it
Skip evidence linkage and just store the status
reason: A capability being SUPPORTED_NOW on the platform registry (e.g. Pocket Studio's own auth) does not mean anything has actually been built for a specific customer project -- Phase 1 generates nothing yet, that is Phase 2. Master Spec §4.4 explicitly forbids inferring implementation from design/capability. Requiring every status to reference real evidence (not just assert a status) is what makes Truth Status trustworthy rather than another unverified claim.
impact: src/lib/orchestration/truth-status-sync.ts, wired into generateProductIntelligence (P1-06). Establishes the pattern later phases' Truth Status updates (real test/build/deployment evidence) will follow.

recommendation: Credential vault uses AES-256-GCM with a fresh random IV per encryption call, keyed by a server-only CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY env var (never in the DB). storeCredential/retrieveCredentialSecret are the only functions that ever touch plaintext; a separate getCredentialMetadata deliberately omits ciphertext/iv/authTag so it is safe to expose broadly.
alternatives: Defer the vault entirely until Phase 3 when real provider connections exist
Use a third-party secrets manager (e.g. AWS KMS/Vault) instead of self-managed encryption
reason: Master Spec §30 requires Integration Requirements tracking now (Phase 1), and §4.7 requires that credentials use 'secure connection flows and references — not ordinary database fields or chat messages' the moment any credential-shaped data exists, even before a real provider is connected in Phase 3. A third-party secrets manager is real infrastructure dependent on a cloud account Phase 1 doesn't require yet (Execution Protocol §8: never block architecture on missing credentials) — self-managed AES-256-GCM with a narrow, tested accessor is the right-sized foundation, and the architecture doesn't preclude swapping in a managed secrets service later.
impact: src/lib/credentials/*, src/lib/product/integrations.ts. Nothing currently calls storeCredential with a real secret (no live provider exists yet), but the pipeline is proven correct via 6 integration tests including tamper-detection (GCM auth tag) and metadata never leaking ciphertext.
risk: Low — encryption correctness verified by round-trip and tamper tests; key management (rotation, HSM-backed storage) remains a Phase 3 concern once real provider credentials actually flow through this path.

recommendation: Billing state changes only through a deterministic state machine (nextBillingState) that mirrors Master Spec §37's failed-payment workflow exactly (grace period precedes restriction, restriction precedes suspension); every organization gets a subscription at creation (Free/Explore, TRIALING) so entitlement checks never special-case a missing subscription; access level is 'full' through grace period and only 'restricted' (never fully blocked) until actual account deletion.
alternatives: Allow billingState to be set directly without going through a state machine
Treat PAST_DUE as immediately restricted
reason: Master Spec §37 explicitly orders the failed-payment workflow (verify -> notify -> retry -> grace period -> restriction -> suspension -> restoration) and requires nonpayment to never trigger immediate restriction or data deletion, and to preserve login/billing/read-only/export/support/cancellation throughout restriction. Enforcing this via an explicit state machine (nextBillingState) rather than ad-hoc field writes makes invalid transitions (e.g. ACTIVE -> DELETED) impossible by construction rather than by convention, and every transition is recorded as a BillingEvent so 'billing provider state is authoritative' is auditable, not just asserted.
impact: src/lib/billing/*. Establishes the pattern Phase 3's real webhook handler will drive (emit BillingLifecycleEvent, never write billingState directly).
risk: Low — no live payment provider exists yet, so nothing production-critical depends on this beyond its own correctness, which 12 tests verify including the full state walk and rejected invalid transitions.

recommendation: Blueprint (Master Spec §23) is a new append-only, full-replace versioned Prisma model (like ProductState, not carry-forward like ProductDNA) with one Json column per required Blueprint facet. generateInitialBlueprint() deterministically derives an initial Blueprint from a project's latest Product State, Product DNA, and the Requirements Engine's re-derived Impact Analysis categories, using a new fixed category-to-template map (src/lib/generation/blueprint-templates.ts) for workflows/screens/actions/dataModels/permissions/businessRules/monetization -- reusing the exact taxonomy P1-06's Requirements Engine already established rather than inventing new domain concepts. validateBlueprint() enforces Master Spec §23's 'Invalid Blueprints may not proceed as successful builds' structurally (schemaVersion, productType, at least one role/screen/requirement, only currently-supported output targets, well-formed data models) and every Blueprint is persisted with its validationStatus and validationErrors regardless of outcome -- INVALID Blueprints are recorded truthfully, never silently discarded or upgraded to VALID. generationMetadata explicitly labels the method as deterministic/template-derived, never AI-authored design, consistent with every other mock/deterministic artifact in this codebase.
alternatives: Build a real AI-backed Blueprint generator now
Make Blueprint carry-forward versioned like ProductDNA instead of full-replace like ProductState
Skip structural validation and always mark Blueprints VALID
reason: Master Spec §61 explicitly defers real AI-model-backed generation to Phase 3; Phase 1-2 use the deterministic mock/template approach throughout (Requirements Engine, Business Model Brief, unit economics), so Blueprint generation follows the same, already-reviewed pattern rather than introducing a new one. Full-replace (not carry-forward) matches how a Blueprint is actually produced -- as one atomic derivation from current Product State, or later a validated Change Set (P2-08) -- never a field-by-field patch. Structural-only validation with honest INVALID recording matches the same 'never overstate' discipline the Level 3 reviewer already verified in Phase 1 (Truth Status, Feasibility Report).
impact: prisma/schema.prisma (Blueprint model, BlueprintValidationStatus enum, BLUEPRINT_VERSION_CREATED event type), src/lib/generation/blueprint.ts, blueprint-templates.ts, blueprint-validation.ts, blueprint-generator.ts. Populates SCREEN/WORKFLOW/DATA_MODEL/ACTION Product Knowledge nodes for the first time, per the note in P1-03's schema comment that Phase 2 generation would be the first system to do so.
risk: Low -- 20 new tests (9 unit, 11 integration against a real database), including an adversarial tenant-isolation check and an explicit INVALID-Blueprint path.
